record.title: Lithuania restricts selected sanctioned Kaliningrad rail cargo, June–July 2022
record.start_precision: day for initial steel policy; actual cement-restriction onset unknown
record.end_precision: upper bound only for observed cement return; steel endpoint unknown
record.scope: Specified goods in rail transit through Lithuania between mainland Russia and Kaliningrad; Kena is documented for returning cement cargo. No universal Kaliningrad blockade or full Lithuanian border closure is inferred.
record.crossings: Kena is named for a cement train; other transit gates are not inferred from the national corridor label
record.direction: Mainland Russia toward Kaliningrad for the observed return; the formal regime concerns transit to and from Kaliningrad
record.movement: Selected sanctioned rail commodities, with steel/ferrous policy evidence and a separately evidenced cement return
record.exceptions: Passengers and non-sanctioned goods continued. Conditional essential-goods rail transit later used commodity quotas; luxury, military/dual-use and road-transport limitations were not universally lifted.
record.imposing_authority: EU sanctions framework; Lithuanian authorities and LTG Cargo implementation
record.enforcement: The ministry documents the initial commodity restriction. LTG and customs report completed train passage by 26 July; a separate Russian regional source reports cement arrival.
record.consequences: No general economic effect is quantified in this round.
record.relationship: REC50-R08-003 concerns Stasylos freight diversion in February 2023 for smuggling control, not the 2022 Kaliningrad commodity restriction. Other northern rows concern roads, persons or later gate schedules; no matching commodity episode was found.
record.status_observation: Historical source evidence only. Unknown endpoint does not establish the present status of the border.
record.current_timing: 2 linked phases; see Chronology phases; do not add overlapping durations
record.current_corrections: 13 July guidance and 22 July operator permission are not observed reopening dates. The early five-wagon “first train” is later described as the second; exact first cement passage is unknown. Passengers and non-sanctioned freight continued.
record.rationale_coding_status: Source-attributed coding accepted after separate challenge; qualifications retained
record.rationale_phase_note: Codes describe the attributed purposes of the specified restriction, not all policies at the same border.

followup_reviews.Researcher: root and verification_recovery, separate original half audits
followup_reviews.Separate challenger: rounds_protocol, separate same-model challenge of both original halves; prior involvement disclosed
followup_reviews.Research finding: The included parent remains a selected-commodity rail restriction, with a formal steel phase and a separately evidenced cement return. It is not a total Kaliningrad blockade or the later Stasylos diversion. Passengers and non-sanctioned freight continued. Cement returned under essential-goods controls and quotas; luxury, military/dual-use and road limitations were not universally removed. P1 retains 17 June legal onset, 20 June confirmation and withheld duration. P2 retains unknown actual cement onset and an observed-return upper bound of 26 July. Neither 13 July guidance nor 22 July permission is an operational endpoint; first/second-train ambiguity remains. Retain official EU-sanctions implementation as the attributed rationale. Russian blockade descriptions remain interested-party characterisations, not an additional independently proven purpose. Interfax’s regional-spokesman account was freshly read. The decisive later BNS body was reread from cache after a fresh timeout, alongside earlier BNS/LRT and operator/ministerial text. BNS republications and LTG statements are not counted as independent news origins; the Commission body remains unavailable. Both phases remain unlocated. Propose removing the cement train’s Kena label from the steel phase and retaining a corridor-level, no-gate-established label. P2’s named Kena evidence is retained without coordinates.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge
followup_reviews.Challenge finding: Challenge packet SHA-256: c6e6fa17f0d3353c233102eec4583df128ecbb23a0ee9696770f763c8bafc444. Per-question challenge findings remain in that packet.

Retain all dates and numerical durations, all held/incomplete phases, exceptions and unlocated geography. Accept14source-metadata refinements without expanding evidence claims.
followup_reviews.Issue dispositions: REC50-R30-NQ04 — Actual cement onset and first passage, steel-specific operational endpoints and gate identity remain unresolved; direct Commission text and the first/second-train sequence are not independently settled.
